1	import fs from 'fs'
2	import path from 'path'
3	
4	/**
5	 * The weekly revisions record (SJAM-521).
6	 *
7	 * An EDITION is the machine-generated account of what changed between two published
8	 * reference-data epochs. It is produced in vynr-data and committed here as a generated
9	 * output — never edited in this repository, exactly like the atlas and education
10	 * artifacts under `lib/`.
11	 *
12	 * HIGHLIGHTS are the one editorial layer, and they are strictly ADDITIVE: a markdown
13	 * file per edition, written by a human after publication, rendered in its own section.
14	 * Nothing in this module lets a highlights file change, hide, or reorder a single
15	 * machine fact — which is what keeps an edition reproducible from its epoch pair after
16	 * a human has annotated it.
17	 *
18	 * "Revisions", not "status" or "journal", and the naming is load-bearing: a status page
19	 * implies uptime reporting this product does not do, and "Journal" is the name of a
20	 * shipped feature inside the app (ADR-0048). An atlas publishes revisions.
21	 */
22	
23	const editionsDirectory = path.join(process.cwd(), 'content/revisions')
24	const highlightsDirectory = path.join(process.cwd(), 'content/revisions/highlights')
25	
26	/**
27	 * Below this many changes, every change is shown expanded by default; at or above it,
28	 * the edition leads with per-category counts and keeps the full set one disclosure
29	 * away. A reader should never have to click to see a small week, and should never be
30	 * handed several hundred rows unasked.
31	 */
32	export const SHOW_ALL_THRESHOLD = 10
33	
34	/** The only edition shape this renderer understands. */
35	export const SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1
36	
37	export type ChangeKind = 'added' | 'removed' | 'updated'
38	
39	export interface EpochEndpoint {
40	  epoch: number
41	  commit: string
42	  committedAt: string
43	  registrySha256: string
44	}
45	
46	export interface RevisionChange {
47	  category: string
48	  kind: ChangeKind
49	  id: string
50	  label: string
51	  datasets: string[]
52	  /** Present only on `updated`. Named public fields; see `otherFieldCount`. */
53	  fields?: string[]
54	  /** Refinements to fields the record deliberately does not name. */
55	  otherFieldCount?: number
56	}
57	
58	export interface CategorySummary {
59	  category: string
60	  added: number
61	  updated: number
62	  removed: number
63	}
64	
65	export interface Edition {
66	  schemaVersion: number
67	  editionId: string
68	  generatedAt: string
69	  from: EpochEndpoint
70	  to: EpochEndpoint
71	  changeCount: number
72	  categories: CategorySummary[]
73	  changes: RevisionChange[]
74	}
75	
76	export class UnsupportedEditionError extends Error {}
77	
78	/**
79	 * Parse and validate one edition.
80	 *
81	 * An edition whose schema this renderer does not know is REFUSED rather than rendered
82	 * partially: a future field could carry a distinction the current markup silently drops,
83	 * and a page that quietly shows less than the record contains is worse than a page that
84	 * says it cannot show it.
85	 */
86	export function parseEdition(raw: string, source: string, expectedId?: string): Edition {
87	  const parsed = JSON.parse(raw) as Partial<Edition>
88	  if (parsed.schemaVersion !== SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION) {
89	    throw new UnsupportedEditionError(
90	      `${source}: schemaVersion ${String(parsed.schemaVersion)} is not ` +
91	        `${SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION}; this renderer would drop fields it does not know.`
92	    )
93	  }
94	  if (!parsed.editionId || !parsed.from || !parsed.to || !Array.isArray(parsed.changes)) {
95	    throw new UnsupportedEditionError(`${source}: missing required edition fields`)
96	  }
97	  // The filename is the URL and the id is what the index links to, so they must be
98	  // the same fact. A mismatch is not cosmetic: the index would render a link to
99	  // `/revisions/<id>` that resolves by looking for `<id>.json` and 404s, and the
100	  // record would advertise an edition nobody can open.
101	  if (expectedId !== undefined && parsed.editionId !== expectedId) {
102	    throw new UnsupportedEditionError(
103	      `${source}: editionId ${parsed.editionId} does not match its filename ` +
104	        `(${expectedId}); the id is the URL, so the two cannot disagree.`
105	    )
106	  }
107	  return parsed as Edition
108	}
109	
110	/** Every published edition, newest epoch first. */
111	export function getAllEditions(): Edition[] {
112	  if (!fs.existsSync(editionsDirectory)) return []
113	  return fs
114	    .readdirSync(editionsDirectory)
115	    .filter((name) => name.endsWith('.json'))
116	    .map((name) =>
117	      parseEdition(
118	        fs.readFileSync(path.join(editionsDirectory, name), 'utf8'),
119	        name,
120	        name.replace(/\.json$/, '')
121	      )
122	    )
123	    .sort((a, b) => b.to.epoch - a.to.epoch)
124	}
125	
126	export function getEdition(editionId: string): Edition | null {
127	  const file = path.join(editionsDirectory, `${editionId}.json`)
128	  if (!isInsideEditions(file) || !fs.existsSync(file)) return null
129	  return parseEdition(fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8'), editionId, editionId)
130	}
131	
132	/**
133	 * The human highlights for an edition, or null.
134	 *
135	 * Returned as raw markdown for the page to render. Absent is the normal case: most
136	 * editions never get one, and an edition without highlights is complete.
137	 */
138	export function getHighlights(editionId: string): string | null {
139	  // Highlights ANNOTATE an edition, so an id with no edition behind it has no
140	  // highlights by definition. Checked here rather than relying on the caller: the
141	  // directory also holds prose about itself, and without this a `README.md` beside the
142	  // notes would render as though it were one edition's editorial panel.
143	  const edition = path.join(editionsDirectory, `${editionId}.json`)
144	  if (!isInsideEditions(edition) || !fs.existsSync(edition)) return null
145	
146	  const file = path.join(highlightsDirectory, `${editionId}.md`)
147	  if (!isInsideHighlights(file) || !fs.existsSync(file)) return null
148	  const body = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8').trim()
149	  return body.length > 0 ? body : null
150	}
151	
152	/**
153	 * Refuse a path that escapes its directory.
154	 *
155	 * `editionId` reaches `getEdition` from a URL segment. Next.js decodes `%2f` before the
156	 * route parameter is handed over, so a crafted id could otherwise traverse out of
157	 * `content/` and read an arbitrary file from the deployment.
158	 */
159	function isInsideEditions(file: string): boolean {
160	  return path.resolve(file).startsWith(path.resolve(editionsDirectory) + path.sep)
161	}
162	
163	function isInsideHighlights(file: string): boolean {
164	  return path.resolve(file).startsWith(path.resolve(highlightsDirectory) + path.sep)
165	}
166	
167	/** Show every change expanded, rather than a summary with the detail folded away. */
168	export function showsEveryChangeByDefault(edition: Edition): boolean {
169	  return edition.changeCount < SHOW_ALL_THRESHOLD
170	}
171	
172	/**
173	 * Changes grouped for rendering, preserving the order the generator emitted.
174	 *
175	 * Deliberately NOT re-sorted: the generator orders by declared category, then kind,
176	 * then label, and re-deriving that here would be a second ordering rule that could
177	 * disagree with the one the record was written in.
178	 */
179	export function groupByCategory(
180	  changes: RevisionChange[]
181	): { category: string; changes: RevisionChange[] }[] {
182	  const groups: { category: string; changes: RevisionChange[] }[] = []
183	  for (const change of changes) {
184	    const last = groups[groups.length - 1]
185	    if (last && last.category === change.category) last.changes.push(change)
186	    else groups.push({ category: change.category, changes: [change] })
187	  }
188	  return groups
189	}
190	
191	/** `+2 · ~1` style counts for a category, omitting the zeroes. */
192	export function summaryParts(summary: CategorySummary): string[] {
193	  const parts: string[] = []
194	  if (summary.added) parts.push(`${summary.added} added`)
195	  if (summary.updated) parts.push(`${summary.updated} refined`)
196	  if (summary.removed) parts.push(`${summary.removed} removed`)
197	  return parts
198	}
199	
200	/**
201	 * What an `updated` change says about itself.
202	 *
203	 * A refinement to fields the record does not name is still reported — as a count, with
204	 * no field names. The alternative, saying nothing, would make a real change invisible;
205	 * naming them would put this repository's internal curation vocabulary on a public page.
206	 */
207	export function describeUpdate(change: RevisionChange): string {
208	  const named = change.fields ?? []
209	  const other = change.otherFieldCount ?? 0
210	  if (named.length && other) {
211	    return `${named.join(', ')}, and ${other} further ${other === 1 ? 'detail' : 'details'}`
212	  }
213	  if (named.length) return named.join(', ')
214	  if (other) return `${other} ${other === 1 ? 'detail' : 'details'}`
215	  return 'refined'
216	}
217	
218	export function formatEpochRange(edition: Edition): string {
219	  return `Epoch ${edition.from.epoch} → ${edition.to.epoch}`
220	}
221	
222	/**
223	 * The calendar date an endpoint's timestamp carries, rendered identically everywhere.
224	 *
225	 * `new Date(iso).toLocaleDateString()` renders in the BUILD MACHINE's zone, so an
226	 * edition committed at `2026-09-04T02:00:00+08:00` reads as 4 September locally and 3
227	 * September on a UTC build host — the same record, two dates. For something whose
228	 * whole claim is reproducibility that is not acceptable.
229	 *
230	 * The date is therefore taken from the timestamp's OWN calendar fields (its leading
231	 * `YYYY-MM-DD`, which is already expressed in the committer's offset) and formatted as
232	 * UTC so no further shift can occur. That is both deterministic and faithful to what
233	 * the commit records — converting to UTC instead would be deterministic but would move
234	 * some editions a day away from the date their commit actually carries.
235	 *
236	 * A string that is not a leading ISO date is returned unchanged rather than run
237	 * through `Date`, which would render "Invalid Date" — an invented answer is worse than
238	 * an unformatted one.
239	 */
240	export function formatDate(iso: string): string {
241	  const match = /^(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})/.exec(iso)
242	  if (!match) return iso
243	  return new Date(`${match[1]}T00:00:00Z`).toLocaleDateString('en-US', {
244	    timeZone: 'UTC',
245	    year: 'numeric',
246	    month: 'long',
247	    day: 'numeric',
248	  })
249	}
250

content.text: I've read the one patch and the code that displays it; now I'm writing up the findings.

findings.claim: The highlight says the 13 photos were "published with the reference data", but the same page also prints a generated line saying no reference-data changes were published in this epoch, so readers see two opposite statements.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader opens /revisions/epoch-968. Because epoch-968.json has changeCount 0, app/revisions/[edition]/page.tsx:237-239 shows "No reference-data changes were published in this epoch." directly under a Highlights panel saying photos were published with the reference data in this epoch. The panel footer also says the record below "is not affected by this note", so the generated line, which is now known to be wrong, stays with nothing next to it to qualify it.

findings.claim: The note promises that "From epoch 969 on, media and map labels appear in the record itself", but nothing in this repo supports that: the edition schema (lib/revisions.ts RevisionChange/Edition, schemaVersion 1) has no media or map-label field, and epoch 969 has not been published yet.
findings.failure_scenario: Epoch 969 is generated by vynr-data and either keeps schemaVersion 1 with no media changes, or adds media under a new schemaVersion. A new schemaVersion makes parseEdition throw UnsupportedEditionError, so the edition is refused. Either way, the epoch-968 page keeps a permanent public claim that the 969 record does not bear out.
